IV. Core Survival Mechanics & Hostile Strategies
Operating overhead (employee wages and maintenance costs) escalates continuously each cycle due to employee seniority and mechanical wear-and-tear.
To expand operations (hiring additional personnel and acquiring advanced machinery costing 8,000,000\text{ points}), companies require massive liquidity infusions.
Substantial production expansion requires issuing additional equity (e.g., issuing 1,000,000 new shares).
If existing shareholders lack capital to purchase their pro-rata share of newly issued equity, their ownership percentage is halved (e.g., from
), triggering an immediate loss of corporate control.
